items.title: Section: The Chapter on Awakening Opens — Two Obstructions Eliminated, Two Wisdoms Gained

items.zh: 云何菩提？謂略說二斷、二智，是名菩提。二斷者，一、煩惱障斷，二、所知障斷。二智者，一、煩惱障斷故，畢竟離垢，一切煩惱不隨縛智；二、所知障斷故，於一切所知無礙無障智。
items.en: What is awakening? In brief, it is two eliminations and two wisdoms — this is called awakening. The two eliminations are: elimination of the afflictive obstruction, and elimination of the cognitive obstruction. The two wisdoms are: because the afflictive obstruction is eliminated, one is forever free of defilement, possessing wisdom no longer bound by any affliction; and because the cognitive obstruction is eliminated, one possesses wisdom unobstructed and unimpeded with respect to everything knowable.

items.zh: 復有異門。謂清淨智、一切智、無滯智。一切煩惱并諸習氣無餘永害，遍一切種不染無明無餘永斷，是名無上正等菩提。

items.title: Section: Omniscience and Instant Comprehension — Complete Knowledge of Every Realm, Event, Category, and Time

items.zh: 一切煩惱并諸習氣畢竟斷故，名清淨智。於一切界、一切事、一切品、一切時智無礙轉，名一切智。界有二種。一者、世界，二者、有情界。事有二種。一者、有為，二者、無為。即此有為、無為二事無量品別，名一切品。謂自相展轉種類差別故，共相差別故，因果差別故，界趣差別故，善、不善、無記等差別故。時有三種。一、過去，二、未來，三、現在。即於如是一切界、一切事、一切品、一切時如實知故，名一切智。
items.en: Because every affliction, together with its habitual traces, is permanently eliminated, this is called pure wisdom. ... Because wisdom operates without obstruction with respect to every realm, every event, every category, and every span of time, this is called omniscience.

items.zh: 無滯智者，暫作意時，遍於一切無礙速疾無滯智轉。不由數數作意思惟，依一作意遍了知故。
items.en: Unobstructed wisdom: the instant attention is directed towards anything at all, unobstructed and swift understanding operates throughout, without needing repeated deliberation — a single act of attention brings complete understanding.

items.title: Section: Why a Buddha's "Freedom from Contention" Means Something Far Deeper Than a Hearer's Own

items.zh: 復有異門。謂百四十不共佛法，及如來無諍願智、無礙解等。是名無上正等菩提。
items.en: There is yet another way of describing this: the one hundred and forty qualities unique to a buddha, together with the Tathāgata's freedom from contention, wisdom that knows as wished, and unimpeded understanding — this too is called unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

items.title: One Hundred and Forty Qualities Unique to a Buddha

items.zh: 百四十不共佛法者，謂三十二大丈夫相、八十隨好、四一切種清淨、十力、四無所畏、三念住、三不護、大悲、無忘失法、永害習氣、一切種妙智。是諸佛法，建立品中當廣分別。
items.en: The one hundred and forty qualities unique to a buddha are: the thirty-two excellent marks of a great being, the eighty accompanying signs, the four kinds of complete purity, the ten powers, the four kinds of fearlessness, the three foundations of mindfulness, the three things never needing to be guarded, great compassion, the faculty of never forgetting, the permanent destruction of habitual traces, and wondrous wisdom perfect in every respect. These buddha-qualities will be elaborated in detail in a later chapter on their own classification.

items.title: Section: Seven Kinds of Supremacy Open — A Physical Basis Beyond Any Other Being's

items.zh: 如是菩提名為最勝。七種最勝共相應故。由是因緣，於諸菩提最為殊勝。云何名為七種最勝？一者、所依最勝，二者、正行最勝，三者、圓滿最勝，四者、智最勝，五者、威力最勝，六者、斷最勝，七者、住最勝。
items.en: Awakening of this kind is called supreme, because it is joined with seven kinds of supremacy. ... First, supremacy of physical basis; second, supremacy of conduct; third, supremacy of fulfilment; fourth, supremacy of wisdom; fifth, supremacy of power; sixth, supremacy of elimination; and seventh, supremacy of abiding.

items.zh: 由諸如來以三十二大丈夫相等莊嚴其身，故名所依最勝。
items.en: Because Tathāgatas adorn their bodies with the thirty-two excellent marks of a great being and the accompanying signs, this is called supremacy of physical basis.

items.title: Five More Kinds of Supremacy — Conduct, Fulfilment, Wisdom, Power, and Elimination

items.zh: 由諸如來自利利他，利益安樂無量眾生，哀愍世間，令諸天人獲得義利利益安樂而行正行，故名正行最勝。
items.en: Because Tathāgatas, benefiting both themselves and others, bringing benefit and ease to countless beings out of compassion for the world, carry out right conduct so that gods and humans attain genuine benefit, ease, and welfare — this is called supremacy of conduct.

items.zh: 由諸如來無上無等四種圓滿，謂戒圓滿、見圓滿、軌則圓滿、淨命圓滿，皆悉成就，故名圓滿最勝。由諸如來無上無等四無礙解，謂法無礙解。義無礙解、訓詞無礙解、辯說無礙解，皆悉成就故，名智最勝。由諸如來無上無等如前所說六種神通皆悉成就，故名威力最勝。由諸如來無上無等一切煩惱習氣永斷，及一切所知障永斷皆悉成就，故名斷最勝。由諸如來多住無上無等三住，謂聖住、天住、梵住，故名住最勝。
items.en: Because Tathāgatas have accomplished four kinds of fulfilment, unsurpassed and unequaled — fulfilment in precepts, in view, in bearing, and in livelihood — this is called supremacy of fulfilment.

items.title: Section: Abiding Supremacy — Why the Fourth Meditative Absorption Survives Every Cosmic Cataclysm

items.zh: 當知此中，空、無願、無相住，及滅盡定住，是名聖住。四種靜慮、四無色定，是名天住。四種無量，是名梵住。
items.en: It should be understood that abiding in emptiness, wishlessness, and signlessness, together with abiding in cessation, is called the noble abiding. The four meditative absorptions and the four formless attainments are called the heavenly abiding. The four immeasurables are called the divine abiding.

items.zh: 於此三住中，如來多住四最勝住。謂於聖住中，多住空住、滅盡定住；於天住中，多住無動第四靜慮住；於梵住中，多住大悲住。
items.en: Among these three abidings, the Tathāgata dwells mostly in four supreme states: within the noble abiding, mostly in the abiding of emptiness and the abiding of cessation; within the heavenly abiding, mostly in the unmoving abiding of the fourth meditative absorption; and within the divine abiding, mostly in the abiding of great compassion.

items.title: Section: Great Compassion — The Buddha's Six-Times-Daily Survey of Every Being's Progress

items.zh: 由是如來晝夜六時，晝三、夜三，常以佛眼觀察世間誰增、誰減，我應令誰未起善根而種善根，廣說乃至我應令誰建立最勝阿羅漢果。
items.en: For this reason, the Tathāgata, six times each day and night — three by day and three by night — constantly observes the world with the buddha-eye, asking whose wholesome roots are growing and whose faults are diminishing: whom should I lead to plant a wholesome root not yet planted? ... and, in detail, all the way to: whom should I now establish in the supreme fruit of arhatship?

items.title: Seven Honorific Titles, Each Rooted in a Different Supremacy

items.zh: 又諸如來所依最勝故，名大丈夫。正行最勝故，名大悲者。圓滿最勝故，名大戒者及大法者。智最勝故，名大慧者。威力最勝故，名大神通者。斷最勝故，名大解脫者。住最勝故，名多安住、廣大住者。
items.en: Because Tathāgatas possess supremacy of physical basis, they are called the Great Being. Because of supremacy of conduct, they are called the Greatly Compassionate One. Because of supremacy of fulfilment, they are called the Great Upholder of Precepts and the Great Upholder of the Teaching. Because of supremacy of wisdom, they are called the Greatly Wise One. Because of supremacy of power, they are called the Greatly Miraculous One. Because of supremacy of elimination, they are called the Greatly Liberated One. Because of supremacy of abiding, they are called the One Who Abides Much and the One of Vast Abiding.

blocks.text: Fascicle 38 contains the chapter on **awakening** (菩提品) and the first part of the chapter on the **lineage of the powers** (力種姓品), the bodhisattva's training: what to learn, how to seek and teach the Dharma, and how to guide others.

"Awakening is two eliminations and two wisdoms": elimination of the afflictive obstruction and of the cognitive obstruction; and the wisdoms that result: **pure wisdom** ("every affliction together with its habitual traces permanently eliminated") and **omniscient wisdom** ("operating without obstruction with respect to every realm, event, category, and time").
"The instant attention is directed towards anything, swift understanding operates throughout, without repeated deliberation."

The qualities unique to a Buddha: thirty-two major marks, eighty minor signs, four purities, ten powers, four fearlessnesses, three foundations of mindfulness, three things never needing to be guarded, great compassion, the faculty of never forgetting, the permanent destruction of habitual traces, and wisdom perfect in every respect. They will be explained in a later chapter.

Of physical basis (the marks); of conduct (benefiting self and others out of compassion); of fulfilment ("in precepts, view, bearing, and livelihood"); of wisdom; of power; of elimination; of abiding.

The noble abidings (emptiness, wishlessness, signlessness, cessation); the heavenly (the absorptions); the divine (the immeasurables). The Tathāgata abides mostly in emptiness, cessation, the "unmoving" fourth absorption, and great compassion.

"Six times each day and night, the Tathāgata observes the world with the Buddha-eye, asking whose wholesome roots are growing and whose faults are dim", and whom to help. Seven honorific titles follow from the seven supremacies.

quiz.q: Awakening is "two eliminations and two wisdoms." How does Venerable Miào Jìng identify the two wisdoms?
options: eliminating the afflictive obstruction is root wisdom; the cognitive, subsequent wisdom
quiz.why: "What is awakening? In brief, it is two eliminations and two wisdoms — this is called awakening." Venerable Miào Jìng: eliminating the afflictive obstruction is really root wisdom; eliminating the cognitive obstruction is really subsequent wisdom.

quiz.q: "Eliminating the cognitive obstruction" — its coarse layers are cut in stages. What does a first-ground bodhisattva cut, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the first ground cuts the "skin-level" coarseness
quiz.why: "The two eliminations are: elimination of the afflictive obstruction, and elimination of the cognitive obstruction." Master Cháng Bǎi: first-ground bodhisattvas cut the "skin-level" coarseness. (Deeper layers are cut later.)

quiz.q: Unobstructed wisdom: "the instant attention is directed." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 暫作意?
options: the mind stirs for a moment
quiz.why: "Unobstructed wisdom: the instant attention is directed towards anything at all, unobstructed and swift understanding operates throughout." Venerable Miào Jìng: 暫作意 — the mind stirs for just a moment.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng count the 140? What do 32 marks plus 80 signs total?
quiz.why: "The one hundred and forty qualities unique to a buddha are: the thirty-two excellent marks of a great being, the eighty accompanying signs …" Venerable Miào Jìng: the thirty-two marks — that's 32; adding the eighty signs, that's 112.

quiz.q: "Awakening of this kind is called supreme." What three kinds of awakening does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish?
options: hearer, solitary-buddha, and buddha awakening — the buddha's is supreme
quiz.why: "Awakening of this kind is called supreme, because it is joined with seven kinds of supremacy." Venerable Miào Jìng: there's hearer awakening, solitary-buddha awakening, and buddha awakening — the buddha's is most supreme.

quiz.q: In the heavenly abiding, the Tathāgata "mostly dwells in the unmoving fourth absorption." Why aren't the first three unmoving, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: thought, joy, and bliss all move — and suffer fire, water, wind calamities
quiz.why: "Within the heavenly abiding, mostly in the unmoving abiding of the fourth meditative absorption." Venerable Miào Jìng: because the first dhyāna has thought, the second joy, the third bliss — all are movement, and they suffer calamities of water, fire, and wind.

quiz.q: The Buddha observes "six times day and night." What is the relation of suffering beings to the Buddha, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: at their worst, suffering beings are closest to the Buddha — he never abandons them
quiz.why: "The Tathāgata, six times each day and night … constantly observes the world with the buddha-eye." Master Cháng Bǎi: suffering beings, at their most painful moments, are closest to the Buddha, because the Buddha never abandons suffering beings.
